Your week in hours

Trap Radar - scan the target

Marketing, algorithms, status buys, convenience markups - they're engineered to strip your freedom. Scan what's tempting you and see the trap for what it is, priced in the one thing you can't get back: hours of your life. Set your wage in Settings for exact hours.

Not tempted - something happened? A thing broke, someone needed you, a bill landed. That is not a trap, and calling it one helps nobody.

Debt Payoff Planner

List what you owe, set what you can throw at it each month, and see the fastest, cheapest way out - with the interest priced in hours of your life.

Where do I find these?
  • Balance - what you still owe today, not what you borrowed. Top of the statement, or the app for that card or loan.
  • Rate APR % - the interest they charge you per year. On a card statement it is usually called purchase APR or interest rate, often on the back or the last page. On a loan it is on the agreement.
  • Min pay $ - the smallest payment they will accept without a late fee. On a card statement it is the minimum payment due.

Do not have the rate to hand? Add the debt anyway with the balance - it still counts what you owe. Come back and fill the rate in when you have the statement, and the numbers sharpen up.

Your way out

Put in what you can throw at debt each month and this shows the payoff date, the interest it costs you, and which order to kill them in. Nothing here changes your budget; it is a projection you can argue with.

Total you can pay toward debt $

This is the whole amount, minimums included - not extra on top of them.

Plot twist: invest instead?

Paying off debt earns a guaranteed return equal to its rate. Investing might earn more - but it's not guaranteed. Here's the honest comparison of aiming that same money at the market instead.

Borrowing to build

A rate you pay against a return you hope for. The interest is a contract; the return is a guess - and this only ever does the arithmetic on both. It will not tell you whether to do it, because it cannot know, and anything that claims otherwise is selling you something.

AccountsWhat's actually in the bank, in your words

Everything else here is built from what you've logged. This is the one place you just state the truth: what's really sitting in each account today. It feeds your net worth and your runway, and it's how "savings" becomes an answerable question - how much is emergency money, how much is the kids'.

And it is the scoreboard. This app never connects to your bank, which means every other figure in it is built from what you chose to type - log less and it looks calmer. This number is the exception, because it comes from outside and you have nothing to gain by inflating it. What it does over months is the honest answer to whether any of this is working. Keep it current and the app can tell you the truth; let it go stale and it can only tell you about your typing.

The real definition: an asset puts money IN your pocket. A liability takes money OUT. Not what you were sold - what's actually true. Net worth counts everything you'd walk away with, but only money-making assets are buying your freedom.

Which areas you want

Turn off anything you do not use and it leaves the menu entirely. Nothing is deleted - whatever you have entered stays exactly where it is and comes straight back if you switch the area on again. Home, Plan, Track and Settings stay put, because an app without them has nothing to do.

What this costs

Nothing, and there is no locked version. No ads, no subscription, no affiliate links pointing you at where to put your money - that would make this the exact thing it was built to fight. It does not see your numbers, so it could not sell them if it wanted to.

Pay what it was worth

One payment, no account, nothing unlocks - you would be paying for the thing you already have. Entirely optional, and the app never asks twice.

Setup & data

Everything lives on this device. Nothing leaves it unless you turn on sync - and sync is encrypted before it goes.

Start over

Wipes the budget, every transaction, your goals and your settings from this browser. There is no server copy and no undo - so save a backup first if there is any chance you will want this back.

Keep a safe backup

Your data lives only in this browser, so clearing your cache or switching devices would wipe it. Save an encrypted backup file you can restore anywhere with your passphrase. The file is scrambled - useless to anyone without the phrase.

A web app cannot write a file to your device on its own - no browser allows it, which is the same rule that stops any page dropping files on your machine. So this watches the clock and asks; saving is one tap.

Interface depth

Guided mode unrolls advanced tools (offense, net worth, sovereignty) only as your Freedom Runway grows, so early on you see just the survival essentials. Switch to Show everything if you want every tool visible now.

Voice & tone

How you want to be held accountable. This is the voice used everywhere - questions, gut-checks, nudges. Forgiving is gentle, Savage pulls no punches. The row below sets how it talks, not how old you are - pick whichever sounds like a person you would listen to.

Chat pacing. The setup chat takes a beat before answering, the way a person would. Turn it off if you would rather it kept up with you.

Starting line

Everybody starts somewhere.

It doesn’t matter whether there’s nothing in your account or plenty. It doesn’t matter whether you’re starting with debt, savings, a paycheck, or a mess you would rather not look at.

This is where you are.

And that’s not a verdict. It’s not a judgment. It’s just your starting line.

What matters is the distance.

Between here and next month. Between here and five years from now. Ten. Twenty. That distance is what this app cares about, and it closes one way: what comes in, what goes out, and what you decide to do about it.

You can call this a budgeting app. That’s not really what it is. It’s an accountability app.

I’m listening.Tell me what comes in and what goes out. I’ll keep track of all of it. Even the boring stuff. Especially the boring stuff.
I’m watching.I’ll show you the patterns hiding in your own numbers - the ones you might rather not look at. No judgment. No sugarcoating.
You can do better.Not as an insult. As the only reason worth opening this.
Now, the part you should hear before you start.

I’m not real. I’m a tool - some arithmetic, some questions you might otherwise avoid, and a memory better than yours. I can’t want this for you. I can’t spend the money for you. I can’t make the decision for you.

That part is yours. All of it. I can think of a million things easier than holding yourself accountable, and most people are doing one of them right now - which costs them their time and their money both.

If you genuinely want the thing you say you want, nobody in here is going to do it for you, and nothing in here will pretend otherwise.

What I will do is keep an honest record. And I won’t flatter it.

Everything you enter stays in this browser. Nothing is uploaded, nothing is sold, and there is no account to create.
